number.why: The served AAD counts match: 7/44 for lactobacilli versus 16/45 for placebo, yielding a reconstructed RR of 0.447443. The published OR and its 95% CI are not an RR estimate or RR interval. However, the ruling incorrectly says the analysis set and follow-up are unstated: the full text explicitly establishes intention-to-treat analysis and planned follow-up through 21 days after the last antibiotic dose, unless AAD occurred earlier.

quotes.span: Among 89 randomized patients, antibiotic-associated diarrhea occurred in seven of 44 patients (15.9%) in the lactobacilli group and in 16 of 45 patients (35.6%) in the placebo group (OR 0.34, 95% CI 0.125 to 0.944; P=0.05).
Analyses of the primary and secondary outcomes were based on the intention-to-treat principle.
The follow-up period was planned to end 21 days after the last administered antibiotic dose, unless AAD occurred before that time.
The primary outcome of the present study was the incidence of AAD during the study period. AAD was defined as three or more liquid stools in a 24 h period.

entry.why: Systemic antibiotic treatment was an explicit population requirement, and study prophylaxis began within its first 48 hours. This establishes antibiotic exposure at entry for the packet's question.

quotes.span: The trial population consisted of hospitalized patients who were anticipated to take at least three days of any systemic antibiotic. Prophylaxis with the study drug or placebo began within the first 48 h of antibiotic treatment.

missed: The full-text ITT and follow-up statements quoted above invalidate the ruling's NOT_STATED analysis-set assessment and its claim that no source states follow-up; they strengthen the served outcome binding without changing the counts or entry verdict. There is also a source-label discrepancy: cache/probiotics-aad-prevention/ft_18026577.txt contains the French abstract span "(RR 0,34, IC 95 % 0,125 à 0,944; p = 0,05)" whereas the English abstract explicitly labels the estimate OR, as quoted above. This discrepancy does not justify using 0.34 as the count-based RR.
